Greetings from Learn with Leaders!

 

We are delighted to invite you to an exclusive 2-part Pre-Med Masterclass Series, led by Harvard student mentor Rohan Tyagi.

 

This series is designed for students, parents, and educators who want to understand what it truly takes to build a strong pre-medical profile — and avoid the common pitfalls that hold most aspiring doctors back.

 

The Pre-Med Masterclass Series:


Led by Rohan Tyagi | Harvard University | Live on Zoom | 9:00 AM – 10:00 AM EDT



Participants can register for one or both sessions — the choice is yours!

 

Session 1: Overview in Medicine — Different Careers, Types of Doctors & Medical School
30th August, 2026

 

Most students who say they want to be doctors have never stopped to ask: which kind of doctor, and why? This session gives students and parents a clear and comprehensive overview of the medical world — from the many career paths available to what medical school actually looks like.

 

Attendees will gain clarity on:
• The many career paths available within medicine and what each involves
• The difference between types of doctors and medical specialisations
• What medical school looks like and how the journey begins
• How to start exploring medicine as a high school student

 

Session 2: Common Mistakes Future Doctors Make (And How to Avoid Them)
6th September, 2026

 

Most pre-med students make the same avoidable mistakes — and most don’t find out until it’s too late. This session breaks down the most common missteps aspiring doctors make in high school, and gives students a clear roadmap for avoiding them.

 

Attendees will gain clarity on:
• The most common mistakes pre-med students make and why they happen
• How to build a pre-med profile that stands out for the right reasons
• What medical school admissions committees are really looking for
• Practical steps to course-correct and get on the right track

 

Mentor Credentials:

 

Rohan Tyagi | Harvard College, Class of 2027 | Neuroscience & Computer Science
Rohan researches neurodegenerative disease mechanisms at the Yankner Lab, Harvard Medical School. He serves as a Teaching Fellow for introductory neuroscience and is an active mentor for first-generation pre-med students.

 

Session Details:

 

Eligibility: Students from Grades 8–12, Parents & Educators
Format: Live, interactive Zoom session
Duration: 60 Minutes per session
Fee: Complimentary

 

Registration Link: https://futuredoctorsprogram.com/masterclass/apply 

 

Seats are limited, and we strongly encourage early registration to secure your spot across both sessions.

 

We look forward to welcoming you to what promises to be an inspiring and practical series for every student with a passion for medicine.

 

Warm regards,
Team Learn with Leaders

LATITUDE AND LONGITUDE
Learning Objective (LO)

Describe and compare how biomes and climates vary across different regions of the world, using examples and maps.

 

Step 1: Recall

Complete the sentences:

Instructions for Learners:
Try to answer all the questions independently without looking at the answer key. Once you have completed the worksheet, check your answers using the Answer Key and correct any mistakes.

Step 1: Recall
The Equator is at 0° latitude.
The Prime Meridian is at 0° longitude.
Lines of latitude run from east to west.
Lines of longitude run from north to south.
Step 2: Climate Detective – Answer Key
1. Which place is closest to the Equator?

Answer: Place A

Reason: Place A is located at 0° latitude, directly on the Equator.

2. Which place is likely to be the coldest?

Answer: Places B and D

Reason: Both B and D are at 60° N, which is much farther from the Equator than A or C. Places at higher latitudes are generally cooler.

3. Which two places have the same longitude?

Answer: None of the places have the same longitude.

A → 0°
B → 60° E
C → 90° E
D → 120° E

Each place has a different longitude.

Note: If you intended this question to have an answer, you should change the map so that two places are placed on the same longitude.

4. Why might two places with the same longitude have different climates?

Answer:
Two places with the same longitude can have different climates because they may have different latitudes. Latitude affects how much sunlight a place receives, making places closer to the Equator generally warmer and places farther from the Equator generally cooler. Other factors such as altitude, distance from the sea and relief can also affect climate.

Critical Thinking
Place A and Place B are on the same longitude but at different latitudes. Predict how their climates might differ. Explain why.

Answer:
If Place A and Place B were on the same longitude but at different latitudes, the place closer to the Equator would generally be warmer, while the place farther from the Equator would generally be cooler. This is because places near the Equator receive more direct sunlight throughout the year. However, other factors such as altitude and distance from the sea can also influence their climates.

Exit Ticket
In three sentences, explain how latitude influences the climate of a place. Is latitude the only factor that affects the climate of a place? Give one other factor that can influence climate.

Answer:
Latitude influences climate because places near the Equator generally receive more direct sunlight and are warmer. Places farther from the Equator generally receive less direct sunlight and are cooler. Latitude is not the only factor that affects climate; altitude is another factor that can influence the climate of a place.
